page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-96GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 8 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. This server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng is in the bottom 10% at 778.19, reflecting the shared CPU allocation and moderate clock speed. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels with a stress-ng score of 6248.71 and a PassMark CPU score of 15683.81. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 829.52 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 56.72 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations and Redis SET performance both rank in the average tier, with Redis achieving 11.95 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of this server lies in its shared CPU model, which limits single-threaded execution speeds but offers high memory density. This makes the configuration qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial RAM without demanding constant, dedicated single-core CPU performance. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, database operations, and moderate multi-threaded processing such as static web serving or lightweight LLM inference using small models.
